sources.title: MQTT Server — The Things Stack
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current TTS documentation at access; page does not pin deployed server release.
sources.locator: MQTT Server intro and note; Subscribing to Upstream Traffic; example uplink topic/payload, lines 19-25, 57-71, 107-155.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the public official documentation page and read the protocol/QoS restriction, upstream topics, tenant-ID caveat, and sample uplink.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: TTS MQTT documentation says MQTT 3.1.1 and QoS 0 only. Topics include tenant ID except on Open Source. This is the app-facing stream; client delivery is subject to QoS 0 semantics.
sources.applicability: Candidate only if the club already uses LoRaWAN/TTS; does not establish club devices, application sample identity, or durable end-to-end delivery.

sources.title: MQTT Version 3.1.1 — OASIS Standard
sources.locator: Abstract/QoS summary lines 53-67; Section 4.3.1 QoS 0 delivery.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the primary OASIS standard, inspected its version/status and QoS descriptions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: QoS 0: no response and no retry; message arrives once or not at all. QoS 1 can duplicate. These are protocol message-delivery modes, not guarantees about semantic observations across devices/apps.
sources.applicability: Defines the meaning of TTS's documented QoS 0 application integration; does not describe the low-power radio/MAC route or the archive's idempotency.

sources.title: Storage Integration — The Things Stack
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current TTS documentation at access; retention is deployment-specific.
sources.locator: How it works, retention, batch delay and Cloud scope, lines 17-34; use cases/configuration lines 62-70.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official TTS documentation and read retention and write timing.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Documented retention: Cloud 30 days, Sandbox 24 hours, Enterprise configurable. Cloud stores only uplinks. Writes are batched and can lag; feature should not serve real-time queries.
sources.applicability: May aid short-gap reconciliation if already enabled; retention is not an adequate club archive and actual TTS deployment/version is unknown.

sources.title: Retrieve Messages — The Things Stack Storage Integration
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current TTS documentation at access; sample schema has historical timestamps.
sources.locator: Retrieve Uplinks using HTTP API, especially JSON example at lines 22-43.
sources.observed_operation: Opened public official retrieval guide and inspected documented sample API result.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Sample exposes root received_at, nested uplink_message.received_at, rx_metadata.time, settings.time/timestamp, session_key_id and f_cnt. Examples distinguish several server/gateway times and a frame counter; no universal sample-time field is promised by this envelope.
sources.applicability: Supports storing transport provenance and keeping observation time separate. A real device payload schema must be inspected before choosing its sample-time field.

sources.title: Troubleshooting Console — The Things Stack
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current TTS documentation at access; no deployed release pinned.
sources.locator: UTC display note and Common Errors: Entity Not Found / Device Not Found and Duplicate Uplink, lines 38-56.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the troubleshooting page, including a focused read around its common errors section.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: An ABP device that resets frame counters may not be found in its existing session and may need reactivation; OTAA avoids that particular problem. A duplicate reception from multiple gateways can be dropped if it arrives outside the deduplication window due to backhaul latency or Packet Broker.
sources.applicability: Illustrates network-server behavior only for TTS/LoRaWAN and specific activation/session conditions. Does not imply the club's gateways or devices use this protocol.

sources.title: LoRaWAN L2 Specification TS001-1.0.4
sources.released_version_or_commit: LoRa Alliance TS001-1.0.4, 2020 specification; official resource page published 2023-09-28 and links errata ERRATA_L2_1_0_4_D2D.
sources.locator: Section 4.3.1.5 Frame counter (PDF page 22/90); also official resource page.
sources.observed_operation: Read official LoRa Alliance resource listing; searched/opened the official PDF's indexed Section 4.3.1.5 text. No device or firmware was accessed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: OTAA successful join resets FCntUp/FCntDown; ABP counters must not reset during device life and must survive power loss. FCntUp increments per uplink subject to retransmission rules; frame counter reuse under the same session keys is prohibited except retransmission; the network server drops retransmitted frame payloads and forwards one instance to the application server.
sources.applicability: Conditional on device LoRaWAN version/activation. FCnt identifies protocol frames, not each sample in a buffered payload and not all downstream delivery.

sources.title: Webhook Retries — The Things Stack
sources.released_version_or_commit: Feature marked new in TTS 3.30.1; Cloud Plus subscription required for TTS Cloud use.
sources.locator: Feature availability/default behavior and retry conditions, lines 21-37; defaults/configuration and schedule lines 68-95.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official TTS webhook retry documentation and read product availability, default, and retry schedule.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Default webhook is tried at most once per application uplink; if endpoint is temporarily unavailable, associated traffic is lost. When enabled, default policy is 7 tries including initial, exponential intervals and jitter; timing values are deployment configuration defaults and endpoint response must be under 10 seconds.
sources.applicability: A conditional alternative to QoS 0 only if the actual deployment already supports/enables it. No account, purchase, or configuration change was made.

sources.title: COPY — PostgreSQL 18 documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 documentation; page lists version 18 as supported and 19 as development at access.
sources.locator: COPY description/default error behavior lines 49-57; HEADER MATCH/ON_ERROR lines 125-152; CSV/null conventions lines 232-251; STDIN and client/server path lines 85-88, 193-196.
sources.observed_operation: Opened PostgreSQL's official versioned COPY documentation and read CSV/header/error/client-input behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: COPY FROM appends to its destination. Default on conversion error is stop; ON_ERROR ignore can discard rows. HEADER MATCH checks header column names/order. CSV blank/null and quoting details matter. STDIN streams via client connection; filename reads from the server's filesystem.
sources.applicability: Supports a controlled PostgreSQL staging design only if PostgreSQL 18 is chosen; COPY itself does not perform staff review, source-file preservation, correction lineage, or observation dedupe.

sources.title: Constraints — PostgreSQL 18 documentation
sources.locator: Unique Constraints and Primary Keys, Section 5.5.3-5.5.4.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official versioned constraints documentation and reviewed uniqueness and null behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Uniqueness applies to the chosen column/key set; by default nulls are distinct in unique constraints unless NULLS NOT DISTINCT is selected. A design must specify a real stable identity and non-null fields if uniqueness is expected.
sources.applicability: Supports proposed intake constraints after station/sample identity is known. It cannot determine the correct sample identity for unknown devices.

sources.title: Transactions — PostgreSQL 18 tutorial
sources.observed_operation: Opened official PostgreSQL transaction tutorial and read atomicity/commit behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A transaction groups related database changes into an all-or-nothing operation; intermediate state is not visible to other transactions before commit.
sources.applicability: Supports a proposed reviewed CSV/staging acceptance transaction; not a product validation or a guarantee over external file storage plus DB without coordinated procedures.

sources.title: Programming Guide — Apache Beam
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current online guide at access; paired code example is pinned to Beam v2.76.0.
sources.locator: Event time, watermarks, windowing, and Section 9.4.2 Handling late data.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the public official Beam guide; queried/read its late-data documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Allowed lateness keeps a window eligible to react to late elements; triggers can emit additional results. Lateness is bounded by policy and does not imply indefinite retention of raw events.
sources.applicability: Analogical design mechanism only; Apache Beam is not recommended as a pilot dependency.

sources.title: TriggerExample.java — Apache Beam source
sources.released_version_or_commit: Beam release tag v2.76.0; release source commit 3862626.
sources.locator: Java source comments and window configuration around lines 1663-1787; zero lateness vs one-day lateness.
sources.observed_operation: Opened GitHub code view at released tag, inspected the examples; code was not downloaded or executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Example explicitly says zero allowed lateness drops late data; ONE_DAY allowed lateness keeps a window open and can emit late panes. Its default trigger, firing/accumulation behavior, and one-day bound are illustrative example choices.
sources.applicability: Concrete released source-code example for a derived aggregation only; not a command to discard archived observations or select a one-day club policy.

sources.title: Spanner Change Stream watermark ordering issue #36470 — Apache Beam
sources.released_version_or_commit: Issue #36470; report says caching/filtering introduced in Beam 2.67 exacerbated it; fixed release cross-reference is v2.69.0.
sources.locator: Issue description root cause lines 163-169; activity fixing/release notes and closure lines 224-282.
sources.observed_operation: Opened public issue, read the affected behavior, root-cause description, and activity timeline.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Spanner change stream partition watermarks could regress because metadata-table watermark updates were reordered; described as exacerbated by 2.67 caching/filtering. This issue concerns a specific Spanner connector, not generic Beam windows or the proposed weather stack.
sources.applicability: Released failure analogue for ordering-sensitive event-time systems; use as caution, not direct evidence the club has the same defect.

sources.title: Beam 2.69.0 release notes
sources.released_version_or_commit: Beam v2.69.0 release tag, short commit 2ca7d21; release page shows 17 Oct; issue chronology is 2025.
sources.locator: Bugfixes list, line 208: Spanner Change Stream stuck issue #36470.
sources.observed_operation: Opened GitHub's official Beam release page and checked the release commit/version and bugfix entry.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Release notes identify the watermark-backwards Spanner Change Stream issue as fixed in 2.69.0. This release fix is relevant only to Beam's connector implementation.
sources.applicability: Confirms the fix/release side of the history chain; does not validate a weather data design.

sources.title: Line protocol reference — InfluxDB 3 Core
sources.released_version_or_commit: InfluxDB 3 Core documentation path; no exact server patch version displayed in the page.
sources.locator: Duplicate points and append-only patterns, lines 254-310.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official InfluxDB 3 Core documentation and read its duplicate-write semantics and recommendations.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A point identity is table + tag set + timestamp. Duplicates merge field sets, and conflicting duplicate fields are not guaranteed to resolve to the latest write; docs recommend append-only unique timestamps.
sources.applicability: Alternative analytics-store design consideration only. If chosen, correction history needs an append-only model; timestamp/tag overwrite cannot be the authoritative correction mechanism.
